# Third-Party Licenses

<!-- Generated by scripts/ci/generate-notices.py. Do not edit: change the pinned build input or
scripts/ci/notices/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md.in and regenerate. `--check` fails when this file is
stale. -->

Xberg itself is licensed under [MIT](LICENSE). This bundle documents every third-party component
that Xberg links against or redistributes in a published artifact, and carries the license text
of each one. Versions and provenance are read from the build inputs that select them — the
native build scripts, the Dockerfiles, the OCR build scripts, the vendored source archives and
the pinned asset checksum manifests — so this file describes the release it ships with rather
than a hand-maintained snapshot.

It covers 16 non-Rust components and 900 Rust crates
resolved from 13 shipped dependency graphs (normal and build dependencies, all
platforms). The Rust crate texts are collected from the same graphs `cargo deny` audits:

- xberg-cli (default)
- xberg-cli --features all,mimalloc
- xberg-py (default)
- xberg-node (default)
- xberg-php (default)
- xberg-ffi (default)
- xberg-jni (default)
- xberg-wasm (default)
- xberg-swift (default)
- xberg-dart (default)
- xberg_nif (default)
- xberg-rb (default)
- xberg-cli --features mcp,mcp-http,api (windows no-heic)

## libheif (HEIF / HEIC / AVIF) — LGPL

- **Feature:** optional `heic` Cargo feature (part of `full`/`formats`). The standalone CLI
  enables `formats`, so its release binaries link `libheif` dynamically.
- **License:** GNU Lesser General Public License, version 3 or later. The complete upstream
  `COPYING` text is reproduced below (`T-` section for the `libheif` rows above).
- **Linking:** **Dynamic**, with one exception (below). Xberg resolves `libheif` via `pkg-config`
  (`-lheif`) against a shared library. The musl CLI container build explicitly disables
  `crt-static` (`RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=-crt-static"`) so the resulting binary loads
  `libheif.so` at runtime rather than embedding it. The embedded source build
  (`embedded-libheif`) feature has been **removed** from `xberg-libheif`. The one static link is
  the macOS PHP extension, described in the next section.
- **Redistribution:** the Linux CLI archives and the `full`/`core` images ship unmodified
  `libheif` shared objects separately from the Xberg executable. The source-built images use
  libheif 1.23.7 from the official release tarball; the musl CLI image uses
  Alpine 3.24.3's shared package. On Windows the CLI archive carries `heif.dll`,
  `libde265.dll` and `aom.dll` as separate replaceable DLLs; that build compiles the vcpkg ports,
  which apply patches to all three libraries, and those patches are listed in the Corresponding
  Source table below. Every shipped library remains replaceable, satisfying LGPL §6.
  Upstream source: <https://github.com/strukturag/libheif>.
- **LGPL-3.0 compliance method (Windows CLI ZIP):** the codecs are linked as shared libraries,
  the §4(d)(1) route, rather than statically. An interface-compatible rebuild of `heif.dll` (or
  `libde265.dll`) dropped in beside `xberg.exe` is loaded instead, which satisfies §4(d)(1)(b),
  and the ZIP ships `GPL-SOURCE-OFFER.txt` for the Corresponding Source (LGPL-3.0 §3, GPL-3.0 §6).
  This file ships in the ZIP as the §4(a) notice; the texts required by §4(b) ship as
  `LGPL-3.0.txt`, `GPL-3.0.txt` and the per-port `*-COPYING` files.
- **Modification notice (LGPL-3.0 §2):** the Windows codecs are not compiled verbatim from the
  upstream tarballs. The vcpkg ports apply the patches named in the Corresponding Source table
  below before building, and Xberg makes no further changes to them.

## libheif codec libraries

Depending on how `libheif` was built, its codec backends are linked shared libraries or
dynamically-loaded plugins. Linux CLI packaging vendors the non-system shared-library closure
required by its `libheif` build; container images install the same codecs from the distro package
manager. Each remains a separate, replaceable shared object and retains its upstream license:

| Library | Role | License (upstream) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| libde265 1.1.3 | HEVC **decode** | LGPL-3.0-or-later |
| libdav1d (Alpine 3.24.3, Debian trixie-20261027-slim) | AV1 **decode** | BSD-2-Clause |
| libaom 3.15.2 and 3.15.3 | AV1 dec/enc | BSD-2-Clause + patent grant |
| libx265 4.3 | HEVC **encode** | **GPL-2.0-or-later** |

Xberg supports both HEIF-family input decoding and optional HEIF image output. `libx265` is
needed only for the latter and is redistributed only when the platform's `libheif` build links
it. The published `core`, `full` and CLI images are decode-only: they build `libheif` with
`-DWITH_X265=OFF` and the release workflow rejects any archive carrying an x265 file name, load
command or symbol, so no GPL codec code reaches them.

The macOS Elixir NIF archive ships `libheif`, `libde265`, `libaom` and `libx265` (built from the
pinned sources with both encoders) as separate sibling dylibs resolved through `@loader_path`,
beside the upstream license texts and a checksum inventory. They remain separate, replaceable
shared objects. `libx265` is licensed **GPL-2.0-or-later**; its exact source is the release
tarball listed for the x265 pin above, also recorded in `sources.tsv` inside the archive with its
`COPYING`. The macOS PHP extension does not contain it.

## PHP macOS extension: static HEIF stack

PIE installs a PHP extension by copying a single file, so sibling dylibs cannot ship with it (a
Homebrew-linked build failed to load on Macs without `libheif`, xberg-io/xberg#2547). Static
linking is therefore used here, and only here: the macOS PHP extension (`xberg.so`, Apple
Silicon, macOS 15 and later) links the following libraries into the extension binary. The Elixir
NIF and every other binding keep shared libraries.

| Library | Version | Role | License (upstream) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| libheif | 1.23.7 | HEIF/HEIC/AVIF container | LGPL-3.0-or-later |
| libde265 | 1.1.3 | HEVC **decode** | LGPL-3.0-or-later |
| libaom | decode profile (see the inventory above) | AV1 **decode** (encoder off) | BSD-2-Clause + patent grant |

The static set is decode-only. Nothing in it can encode, and no GPL code is linked: `libx265`
and every other encoder are excluded, so HEIF **output** is unavailable in this extension (Xberg
reports an encoder-unavailable warning, as the macOS Python wheel and Node packages already do).
HEIC and AVIF decoding is unaffected.

- **Source and provenance:** every component is built unmodified from its pinned upstream
  release tarball. The URLs and SHA-256 checksums are in
  [`scripts/ci/build-macos-heif-deps.sh`](scripts/ci/build-macos-heif-deps.sh) (profile
  `php-static`) and in `sources.tsv`, shipped inside each macOS PHP archive beside the upstream
  license texts (`libheif-*-COPYING`, `libde265-*-COPYING`, `libaom-*-LICENSE`,
  `libaom-*-PATENTS`), the GNU GPL v3 text (`GPL-3.0.txt`, which LGPL-3.0 §4(b) requires beside
  the LGPL text for the combined work) and a `notices.sha256` list. Xberg's own `LICENSE` and
  this file ship there too; the codec texts are reproduced below.
- **Relinking (LGPL-3.0 §4):** the complete source of the extension is public
  (<https://github.com/xberg-io/xberg>, `crates/xberg-php`, MIT). To rebuild it against your own
  modified `libheif` or `libde265`, reproduce the release job `php-extension` in
  [`.github/workflows/publish.yaml`](.github/workflows/publish.yaml) on an Apple Silicon Mac with
  macOS 15 or later:
  1. Check out the release tag (`git checkout v<version>`) and install the PHP version you
     target (8.3, 8.4 or 8.5, non-thread-safe), Rust from `rust-toolchain.toml` and Xcode
     command-line tools.
  2. Replace the pinned tarball URL and `*_SHA256` of the library you changed in
     `scripts/ci/build-macos-heif-deps.sh`, then build the static stack into an empty directory:
     `XBERG_HEIF_PROFILE=php-static XBERG_HEIF_PREFIX=<new empty dir>
     MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 bash scripts/ci/build-macos-heif-deps.sh`. The script requires
     arm64, that exact deployment target and a fresh prefix, and fails otherwise.
  3. Export `PKG_CONFIG_PATH=<prefix>/lib/pkgconfig` and `SYSTEM_DEPS_LIBHEIF_LINK=static`, then
     build the extension the way the release does: `scripts/build-out-of-workspace.sh xberg-php
     xberg_php <checkout>` from the `build-php-extension` action of
     [`xberg-io/actions`](https://github.com/xberg-io/actions) (`v1`). It copies `crates/xberg-php`
     out of the workspace, resolves its dependencies from crates.io at the release version and
     builds the `xberg_php` library with the crate's default features; the resulting
     `libxberg_php.dylib` is the `xberg.so` the archive carries.
  4. Check it with `scripts/ci/verify-php-macos-extension.sh` (it needs an archive;
     `scripts/ci/stage-php-macos-notices.sh` builds one around your binary) and load it with
     `php -d extension=/path/to/xberg.so`, replacing the file PIE installed.
- **Gate:** the release workflow runs `scripts/ci/verify-php-macos-extension.sh` on every macOS
  PHP archive. It rejects any import outside `/usr/lib` and `/System/Library` (including Homebrew
  paths), any libheif or codec import, a deployment target above macOS 15.0, and a missing or
  altered notice.

## libwpd + librevenge (WordPerfect) — MPL-2.0

- **Feature:** the `xberg-libwpd` crate, consumed by `xberg`'s `wordperfect` feature (included in
  `formats`, `full` and `windows-target`). Desktop only (Linux, macOS and Windows).
- **License:** libwpd 0.10.3 and librevenge 0.0.6 are dual-licensed
  **MPL-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1+**. Xberg builds and links them under the **MPL-2.0** arm; both
  `COPYING.MPL` texts are reproduced below.
- **Linking:** **Static, from source.** `xberg-libwpd` vendors the upstream librevenge and libwpd
  release tarballs as committed `.tar.gz` archives under `crates/xberg-libwpd/vendor/`; its build
  script decompresses them (checksum-verified at extract time), compiles them from source, and
  statically links them together with a small C++ shim. MPL-2.0 is file-level (weak) copyleft and
  explicitly permits static linking into a larger, differently-licensed work; obligations are
  limited to keeping the libwpd/librevenge source and any modifications to their files available
  under MPL-2.0 and preserving license notices. No copyleft reaches Xberg's MIT core or the
  language bindings. The LGPL arm is intentionally not used, as LGPL static linking would impose
  relink/object-file obligations on redistributed binaries.
- **Modifications:** none; both libraries are built from unmodified upstream source. Upstream
  source: <https://libwpd.sourceforge.net/>.
- **Boost (build-time headers) — BSL-1.0:** the C++ shim compiles against a `bcp`-extracted
  header-only subset of the Boost C++ Libraries (1.90.0), vendored as
  `crates/xberg-libwpd/vendor/boost-subset.tar.gz` and decompressed at build time. Boost is
  licensed under the **Boost Software License 1.0** (BSL-1.0), a permissive license whose only
  obligation is preserving the license text; no copyleft or attribution-in-binary obligation
  reaches Xberg. Boost headers are a build-time dependency only — no Boost code is redistributed
  in Xberg binaries.

## ONNX Runtime (OCR / ML features) — MIT

- **Feature:** optional (`paddle-ocr`, `layout-detection`, `embeddings`, `reranker`,
  `auto-rotate`, transcription). License: MIT. Linked dynamically (system
  `libonnxruntime.so`) in the musl/container builds; bundled per the `ort-bundled` feature
  (official Microsoft binaries) otherwise.
- **Redistribution:** the official release archives at 1.23.2 and 1.24.2 are pinned by
  SHA-256 in `scripts/ci/actions/setup-onnx-runtime/checksums.sha256`; the Alpine 3.24.3
  CLI image installs its distribution package instead. The upstream MIT text is reproduced below.

## PDFium (PDF rendering) — BSD-3-Clause

- **Feature:** `pdf-pdfium`. The engine `dlopen`s `libpdfium.so`/`pdfium.dll`/`libpdfium.dylib`
  from the release archive at PDFium revision 7678; the revision and every asset
  digest are pinned in `scripts/pdfium-runtime-checksums.sha256`.
- **License:** BSD-3-Clause, reproduced from `crates/xberg-pdfium-render/include/LICENSE.pdfium`
  below.

## mimalloc (musl CLI) — MIT

The musl CLI statically links the native mimalloc allocator through the `mimalloc` Rust crate and
`libmimalloc-sys`. The wrapper and bundled C allocator use the same MIT terms with the copyright
notices carried in those crates' license texts, reproduced below under the Rust entries.

## Tesseract OCR + Leptonica

- **Feature:** `xberg-tesseract` builds Tesseract 5.5.4 and Leptonica
  1.87.0 from checksum-verified source archives when `build-tesseract` or
  `build-tesseract-wasm` is enabled; the `core`/`full` images build the same versions through
  `scripts/ci/install-system-deps/build-ocr-linux.sh`. The Debian trixie-20261027-slim package is also
  installed in those images for its language data.
- **Licenses:** Tesseract is Apache-2.0; the exact upstream text is preserved in
  [`crates/xberg-tesseract/licenses/tesseract-LICENSE`](crates/xberg-tesseract/licenses/tesseract-LICENSE)
  and reproduced below. Leptonica is BSD-2-Clause; the exact upstream notice is preserved in
  [`crates/xberg-tesseract/licenses/leptonica-LICENSE`](crates/xberg-tesseract/licenses/leptonica-LICENSE)
  and reproduced below.
- **Linking:** both native libraries are built from their checksum-verified source archives and
  statically linked into the consuming artifact. Their permissive licenses permit static linking
  when the license texts and notices accompany redistribution.
- **Model redistribution:** `eng.traineddata` is redistributed from `tessdata_fast` at the
  revision pinned in `crates/xberg-tesseract/build.rs` after checksum verification. `tessdata_fast`
  uses the same Apache-2.0 license text as Tesseract, so the preserved Tesseract license covers
  the model artifact.
- **tessdata_best:** the `core-best`/`full-best` images also redistribute `tessdata_best` models
  (Apache-2.0) for their OCR languages, downloaded at the revision and SHA-256 digests pinned in
  `crates/xberg/src/ocr/tessdata_download/pins.rs` and checked against
  `scripts/ci/tessdata/tessdata_best.sha256`. The repository's `LICENSE` at that revision, verified
  by the same manifest, ships beside them at `/usr/local/share/licenses/tessdata_best/LICENSE`.

## Embedded fonts

The PDF engine embeds fonts through `include_bytes!`; the DejaVu license requires its notice in
all copies and in unmodified form, which is why the assets are shipped byte-identical and listed
with their digests:

| Font | Asset | sha256 | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DejaVu Sans | `crates/xberg-native-pdf/src/fonts/assets/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf` | `0d977336a6d5fba3` | Bitstream-Vera |
| DejaVu Sans | `crates/xberg-native-pdf/src/fonts/assets/DejaVuSans.ttf` | `abdc775b21b1bc47` | Bitstream-Vera |
| Droid Sans Fallback | `crates/xberg-native-pdf/src/fonts/assets/DroidSansFallbackFull.ttf` | `acb6440a713d880a` | Apache-2.0 |
| Noto Emoji | `crates/xberg-native-pdf/src/fonts/assets/NotoEmoji-Regular.ttf` | `415dc62903785741` | OFL-1.1 |

## Rust crate dependencies

900 crates from 13 shipped dependency graphs, 518 distinct license texts. Each crate
appears under every distinct license text it ships, and a crate that ships no license file of its
own is covered by the canonical SPDX text for its declared expression. Build-only dependencies are
listed because they are part of the audited graph, not because their code is redistributed.
`cargo deny check licenses` enforces `deny.toml` on the same graphs.

## License texts

Every distinct license text appears once. `T-` identifiers are the first twelve hex digits of the
text's sha256, so a text keeps its identifier across regenerations.
